question: In a transformer, insulation resistance test is carried out to measure:

options.text: the inductance between different parts of the transformer
the resistance of the insulation between windings and core

solution:
The correct answer is __the resistance of the insulation between windings and core**(Option 2)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Insulation resistance test__ is a fundamental electrical test.
 
• The test measures the resistance offered by the insulation to the flow of current.
 
• It helps ensure that the insulation between windings and the core is intact and has no leakage.
 
• This test is essential to prevent electrical faults in transformers.
 
• It is a preventive maintenance tool to detect insulation deterioration early.
 
• The test is performed using a device called a megger.
 
• It ensures the safety and reliability of transformer operations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Inductance:**
 
 
• Inductance is the property of a circuit or component that opposes changes in current flow.
 
• It is not measured by an insulation resistance test.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Flux:**
 
 
• Magnetic flux refers to the measure of magnetic field strength through a given area.
 
• It is unrelated to insulation resistance testing.
 
 
 
• **Frequency:**
 
 
• Frequency is the rate at which an alternating current changes direction.
 
• It is not determined in an insulation resistance test.
